name: Tessera Resonance Projector RP-5 'Tuning Fork'
description:
A sonic weapon that projects a focused infrasonic beam capable of inducing resonance in solid structures, organic tissue, and cybernetic implants. The RP-5 fires a directed sound pulse at frequencies between 7-18 Hz — below the threshold of human hearing but within the range that causes involuntary physiological responses including nausea, disorientation, bowel disruption, and panic.

Tessera developed the Resonance Projector as a crowd-control tool, but its applications have expanded far beyond non-lethal suppression. At maximum power, the RP-5's infrasonic beam can induce structural resonance in buildings, causing micro-fractures that accumulate into catastrophic failure over sustained exposure. Against personnel, high-power settings can rupture blood vessels, dislodge retinas, and stop hearts.

The weapon is invisible and nearly silent — targets experience its effects without understanding their source. This makes the Resonance Projector uniquely terrifying. Victims feel their bodies betraying them, their organs vibrating, their vision blurring, with no visible attacker and no audible weapon.
legality: Non-lethal classification at low power; Military restricted at full power
specifications: caliber: N/A — focused infrasonic beam effective_range: 10-300 meters rate_of_fire: Continuous beam, adjustable power capacity: N/A — limited by power supply weight: 8.4 kg power_source: Integrated power cell, 30 minutes continuous at full power
tactical_use: The Tuning Fork is deployed for area denial, crowd dispersal, and non-lethal incapacitation at low power settings. At full power, it becomes a lethal weapon that kills without leaving ballistic evidence. Intelligence operatives have used the RP-5 to induce 'natural' deaths — heart failure, stroke, aneurysm — that pass autopsy examination unless the examiner specifically tests for resonance damage to tissue. The weapon's dual-use nature makes it politically versatile — the same tool that disperses a protest at low power can assassinate a dissident at full power.
cultural_context: The existence of sonic weapons has created a new form of paranoia in GLMZ. When people feel unexplained nausea, dizziness, or panic, they wonder if they are being targeted by a weapon they cannot see or hear. This phenomenon — called 'the hum' in popular culture — has become a catch-all explanation for everything from genuine weapon use to psychosomatic symptoms. Tessera neither confirms nor denies which incidents involve their technology.
story_hooks: Residents of a Tier 2 block have been experiencing chronic nausea, insomnia, and nosebleeds for weeks. They believe they are being targeted by a sonic weapon, but no device has been found. The symptoms are real — the cause could be an RP-5, industrial equipment, or something else entirely.

A Tessera engineer has leaked specifications for an RP-5 variant tuned to the resonant frequency of specific cyberware models. The weapon would selectively destroy augmentations without harming organic tissue — or it would, if the frequency targeting were precise enough.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular device resembling a hybrid between a directional microphone and a compact rifle. The chassis tapers toward a wide, parabolic emission array at the forward end. Despite its weapon function, it reads as clinical and almost musical — the parabola suggests audio equipment rather than lethal hardware. Asymmetrical design with a pronounced shoulder mount and stabilizing fins.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 68 cm | Emission array diameter: 22 cm | Width at grip: 8 cm | Height with rail mounts: 14 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively heavy for its size — 8.4 kg distributed toward the rear creates a forward-weighted balance designed for sustained aiming. Feels purposeful and solid in-hand despite the slim profile. The weight suggests precision over portability.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite chassis with titanium reinforcement struts around the emission array. Internal framework of hardened aluminum for vibration dampening.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with a subtle brushed texture that resists fingerprints and reflection. The parabolic array features a darker, almost iridescent anodized finish that shifts faintly purple-black under dramatic lighting — suggesting the exotic resonance technology within.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary body with deep violet-black emission array. Accent trim in brushed titanium along the top rail and grip area. Subtle cyan LED status indicators (power, frequency, resonance lock) arranged vertically along the left side.
physical_description.grip_texture: Ergonomic rubberized polymer with shallow vertical ribs for secure purchase. Textured enough to prevent slipping during sustained operation, but with a soft matte finish that feels almost clinical. Small pressure-responsive pads at thumb and trigger-finger positions.
distinctive_features: Wide parabolic resonance emitter at muzzle — the acoustic 'mouth' that projects the invisible beam
Three stacked cyan LED indicators on left rail showing power status, active frequency band, and resonance lock confirmation
Delicate frequency tuning dial (ring-style) positioned just behind the emitter — labeled with Hz ranges in elegant sans-serif numerals
Heat dissipation fins along the top and sides of the emission array, barely visible but textured to the touch
Integrated pressure sensor pad on the fore-grip that modulates beam intensity based on grip pressure
Telescoping stabilization arm that deploys from the underside for sustained aiming
Faint TESSERA holographic logo etched into the charging port cover — visible only at oblique angles
Wear pattern evidence: minor scuff marks on the grip rubber, micro-fractures in the matte finish where hands have held it repeatedly
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA branding appears as a discrete holographic inlay on the left side of the chassis, visible only at 45-degree angles. Serial number stamped in micro-text on the charging port panel. A tiny Φ symbol (QUANTA currency mark) engraved near the rail — indicating high market value.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units range from pristine corporate inventory (used only in training) to well-maintained security contractor builds with minor cosmetic wear. Battle-worn examples show scuffed finish, stress fractures around the emission array, and replacement grip wraps. Powdust from industrial sites or residue from extended use in confined spaces often visible in the fin gaps.
